plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 (ZnS/MgF2 Single-Cavity Defect-Engineered Dual-Band Filter) which failed with 0 physically valid candidates due to material_data issues. Three new routes proposed: (1) Alternative material pair Ge/YbF3 with expanded thickness bounds and 20-layer defect-cavity topology, (2) Reduced 16-layer ZnSe/ThF4 stack for improved numerical stability, (3) Double-cavity 22-layer Ge/YbF3 design for better passband isolation. All routes expand thickness bounds by 20% from previous [200,1200]nm to [160,1440]nm, add NaN guards, and maintain the defect-engineered dual-band scientific principle while changing materials and topology to address material_data failure.

routes.title: Ge/YbF3 Defect-Cavity Dual-Band Filter with Expanded Thickness Bounds
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing ZnS/MgF2 with Ge/YbF3 material pair will resolve material_data failures while maintaining defect-cavity dual-band transmission physics. Germanium provides high index contrast in mid-IR, YbF3 provides low index with verified optical constants. Expanded thickness bounds [160,1440]nm ensure feasible initialization points.
routes.design_principle: Single defect-cavity multilayer with alternating high/low index layers. Two defect layers positioned to create transmission peaks at 3.30 μm and 4.25 μm center wavelengths. Quarter-wave optical thickness scaling for Bragg mirrors surrounding defect cavities.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/YbF3]_5 | Ge_defect1 | [YbF3/Ge]_3 | YbF3_defect2 | [Ge/YbF3]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total 20 finite layers.
design_variables: Defect layer positions fixed by topology
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and YbF3 are conventional IR dielectrics with deposition heritage
Thickness bounds [160,1440]nm expanded 20% from previous route
theory_basis: Defect-cavity resonance theory for dual-band transmission
expected_advantages: Ge/YbF3 pair has better documented IR optical constants than ZnS/MgF2
Expanded thickness bounds prevent initialization failures
known_risks: Ge has higher absorption in mid-IR than ZnS
YbF3 mechanical properties may differ from MgF2
Defect-cavity coupling may create unwanted sidebands
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer defect-cavity dual-band filter on CaF2 substrate under air incidence. Layer sequence: Air | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | Ge_defect | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3_defect | Ge | YbF3 | Ge | YbF3 | CaF2. All 20 finite layer thicknesses are optimization variables with bounds [160, 1440] nm. Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350nm and 4200-4300nm bands. Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100nm and 4450-5000nm bands. Use TMM solver with NaN guards and constraint-violation logging. No metal layers. Normal incidence, unpolarized. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Changed material pair from ZnS/MgF2 to Ge/YbF3 to address material_data failure. Expanded thickness bounds by 20% from [200,1200]nm to [160,1440]nm per feedback directive. Maintained 20-layer defect-cavity topology.

routes.title: ZnSe/ThF4 Reduced 16-Layer Dual-Band Filter for Numerical Stability
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 20 to 16 will improve numerical stability and reduce material_data failure probability. ZnSe/ThF4 material pair offers verified mid-IR optical constants with lower absorption than Ge-based designs.
routes.design_principle: Simplified defect-cavity topology with fewer Bragg mirror pairs. Two defect cavities maintained for dual-band operation. Reduced total optical thickness improves convergence.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [ZnSe/ThF4]_4 | ZnSe_defect1 | [ThF4/ZnSe]_2 | ThF4_defect2 | [ZnSe/ThF4]_4 | CaF2 substrate. Total 16 finite layers.
design_variables: Defect layer positions fixed by topology
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count 16 <= 24 limit with 8-layer margin
ZnSe and ThF4 are conventional IR dielectrics
Thickness bounds [160,1440]nm expanded 20% from previous route
theory_basis: Reduced layer count improves numerical conditioning
expected_advantages: Fewer layers reduce cumulative numerical error
ZnSe/ThF4 pair may have better registry coverage than ZnS/MgF2
8-layer margin under 24-layer limit allows future complexity increase
known_risks: Fewer Bragg pairs may reduce out-of-band blocking
ThF4 less common than MgF2 in deposition facilities
May not achieve same spectral slope steepness as 20-layer design

routes.title: Ge/YbF3 Double-Cavity 22-Layer Dual-Band Filter with Enhanced Isolation
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Double-cavity topology with 22 layers will provide better passband isolation between 3.3 μm and 4.25 μm bands compared to single-cavity design. Ge/YbF3 material pair addresses previous material_data failure.
routes.design_principle: Two separate defect cavities with dedicated Bragg mirror sections for each passband. Increased layer count allows steeper spectral slopes and better out-of-band blocking while staying under 24-layer limit.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/YbF3]_6 | Ge_defect1 | [YbF3/Ge]_4 | Ge_defect2 | [Ge/YbF3]_6 | CaF2 substrate. Total 22 finite layers.

manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count 22 <= 24 limit with 2-layer margin
Ge and YbF3 are conventional IR dielectrics
Thickness bounds [160,1440]nm expanded 20% from previous route
22 layers approaches manufacturability limit per evidence

expected_advantages: Higher layer count enables steeper spectral slopes
Ge/YbF3 pair addresses material_data failure from route_03
known_risks: Increased complexity may cause convergence difficulties
Ge absorption may reduce peak transmittance
